overall_summary: Crypto tone is heavy as the Senate shelves the Clarity Act, Saylor opens the door to possible Strategy BTC sales, and exchanges shut amid collapsing volume. ETF outflows and the break below 64k add pressure, even as softer oil and yields give modest macro support. Traders are in wait-and-see mode ahead of tomorrow’s FOMC.
key_points: Saylor opens door to BTC sales
BitMEX and BitMart shut on volume collapse

items.title: Senate Shelves Crypto Clarity Act for Now
items.summary: The U.S. Senate has delayed floor action on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act to prioritize Russia sanctions and nominations. With the August recess starting August 8, this leaves little time and makes 2026 passage uncertain amid ongoing ethics disputes. Traders should care because stalled market structure rules keep big institutions cautious and remove a potential bullish catalyst for Bitcoin adoption.
items.impact: Increases regulatory uncertainty and weighs on sentiment

items.title: Bitcoin Drops Below $64K on Kospi Crash
items.summary: Bitcoin fell roughly 2.5 percent to around 63,400 dollars as South Korea's Kospi index plunged over 10 percent on chip stock fears, hitting circuit breakers and sparking global risk-off. The move dragged alts lower and aligned with the Clarity Act delay ahead of the Fed decision. Traders should watch this correlation because equity stress is spilling directly into crypto and testing key supports.
items.impact: Short-term downside pressure with elevated volatility risk

items.title: $100M Liquidated as BTC Breaks $64K Again
items.summary: About 100 million dollars in leveraged crypto positions were wiped out in a single hour as Bitcoin slipped under 64,000 dollars for the third time this week. Longs took most of the pain in the risk-off cascade tied to Asian equities. Traders should care because repeated leverage flushes around this level can either clear weak hands for a bounce or signal further breakdown if support fails.
items.impact: Leverage reset that may stabilize or amplify next move

items.title: Saylor Opens Door to Strategy Bitcoin Sales
items.summary: Michael Saylor said Strategy may sell Bitcoin or issue stock to fund buybacks of its STRC preferred shares when they trade at a discount. The firm aims for stable preferred trading and has already been repurchasing shares. This matters to traders because even conditional sales from one of Bitcoin's largest corporate holders introduce potential supply overhang that contrasts with its prior pure accumulation stance.
items.impact: Possible future selling pressure from major holder

items.title: BitMEX and BitMart Shut Amid Volume Collapse
items.summary: BitMEX will permanently close in September and BitMart is winding down trading, joining other firm failures as centralized exchange volumes hit multi-year lows around 1 trillion dollars monthly. Analysts blame fading retail speculation and rising compliance costs. Traders should note this signals industry consolidation where only scaled compliant platforms survive, underscoring weak retail participation.
items.impact: Highlights sector stress and lower retail activity

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Post $11.6M Net Outflow
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw roughly 11.6 million dollars in net outflows on July 27, led by BlackRock's IBIT, after prior weekly inflows. This comes as price weakens and macro uncertainty builds before the Fed. Flows remain a key gauge of institutional demand, so even modest redemptions flag caution among big money.
items.impact: Mild check on institutional buying pressure

items.title: FOMC Decision Tomorrow Under Chair Warsh; Hold Favored
items.summary: The Fed's two-day FOMC meeting is underway with the rate decision due Wednesday at 2pm ET. Markets price a high probability of holding the funds rate at 3.50-3.75 percent for a fifth straight meeting, though oil-driven inflation risks have kept some hike odds alive around 30-35 percent. New Chair Kevin Warsh has stressed no tolerance for high inflation and less forward guidance, so the statement and any press conference comments will be closely watched for hawkish signals. Crypto traders should care because a hold with dovish tilt supports risk assets while any hike talk or hawkish surprise could pressure Bitcoin and equities.
items.impact: High volatility around decision; hold likely mild positive for crypto

items.title: Durable Goods Orders Miss Big; Core Holds Up on AI
items.summary: June durable goods orders rose just 0.3 percent, well below the 1.6 to 2.1 percent forecasts, after a sharp prior drop. Ex-transportation orders gained 0.6 percent and core capital goods excluding aircraft rose about 0.9 percent, pointing to resilient business investment tied to the AI buildout. The soft headline may feed into softer Q2 growth estimates but the underlying strength limits recession fears. Traders watch this as a read on manufacturing and capex heading into the Fed decision and Thursday GDP.
items.impact: Mixed data; limited immediate market move but supports soft-landing view

items.title: Oil Falls Sharply on US-Iran Strike Pause
items.summary: Crude prices dropped as the US and Iran paused strikes after recent escalations, reversing some of the war premium that had pushed oil higher and lifted inflation fears. Lower energy costs ease pressure on consumer prices and reduce the odds of an immediate Fed hike. This improves risk sentiment globally and has contributed to a softer dollar tone. Crypto benefits from the de-escalation and lower inflation path as it reduces the chance of tighter policy.
items.impact: Eases rate-hike fears and supports risk assets including Bitcoin

items.title: Atlanta Fed GDPNow Slips to 1.6 Percent for Q2
items.summary: The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model lowered its Q2 2026 real GDP growth estimate to 1.6 percent after the latest data including durables. This is soft relative to earlier readings and consensus around 1.8-2.3 percent for the advance release due Thursday. Soft growth keeps the Fed on hold but also highlights cooling momentum after Q1's 2.1 percent. Traders should note it as a key input for rate path expectations and overall risk appetite into the GDP print.
items.impact: Supports hold but signals slower growth; watch Thursday GDP

items.title: 10-Year Yield Eases to Around 4.65 Percent; DXY Steady
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield pulled back toward 4.65 percent after recent highs near 4.7 percent, while the dollar index hovered near 101.5. Mortgage rates remain elevated around 6.58 percent for the 30-year. Softening yields reflect lower oil and tempered hike bets ahead of the Fed. A stable-to-softer dollar and yields environment is generally supportive for crypto and risk assets by easing financial conditions.
items.impact: Easier financial conditions positive for Bitcoin and equities

items.title: Today's Data: Trade Balance, Consumer Confidence, Home Prices
items.summary: Tuesday brings the advance goods trade balance for June, Conference Board consumer confidence for July, Case-Shiller home prices, and other releases including ADP weekly employment. Confidence is expected to edge up from 91.2 toward 92, while trade data will update the deficit picture ahead of full GDP. These fill in the pre-FOMC puzzle on consumer strength and external balances. Any big surprise could shift Fed pricing or risk sentiment before Wednesday's decision.
items.impact: Potential short-term volatility; feeds into Fed and growth views

items.title: Gulf Backs Oman Plan for Voluntary Hormuz Fees
items.summary: Oman has presented a proposal, now backed by Gulf states, for a regional mechanism managing the Strait of Hormuz with voluntary fees modeled on the Malacca Strait. This comes as the US-Iran military pause holds for multiple nights, with Trump saying there are good talks but warning strikes resume if talks fail. Oil has tumbled further, with Brent around the mid-80s. Traders should care because successful reopening of this chokepoint, which normally handles 20 percent of global oil, would crush the energy risk premium, ease inflation fears, and spark a broad risk-on move across equities and crypto.
items.impact: Lower oil prices and reduced geopolitical premium support risk assets

items.title: Houthis Target Saudi East-West Oil Pipeline Route
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed drone and missile strikes on Saudi crude transport infrastructure linking eastern oil fields to the Red Sea export hub at Yanbu, plus earlier hits on Aramco sites. Red Sea shipping through Bab el-Mandeb has dropped to multi-month lows as a result. This expands the Iran-linked war into a second energy chokepoint just as Hormuz diplomacy advances. For traders, it keeps a floor under oil prices and war-risk insurance, offsetting some de-escalation gains and reminding markets that proxy attacks can quickly reverse the risk-on move.
items.impact: Sustains oil supply fears and shipping disruptions via Red Sea

items.title: Trump Hosts Zelensky and Netanyahu Amid Dual Wars
items.summary: President Trump is meeting Ukrainian President Zelensky and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu in Washington today, both in town for Senator Lindsey Graham's funeral. Zelensky is prioritizing air defense interceptors and Patriot production licenses as Ukraine shows battlefield gains, while Netanyahu seeks support amid strained ties and Iran war complications. These talks sit at critical junctures for both conflicts. Crypto and risk traders watch for any signals on US aid levels, peace frameworks, or Middle East escalation that could swing safe-haven flows and overall risk appetite.
items.impact: Outcomes on aid and diplomacy will set near-term risk tone

items.title: Oil Extends Slide as US-Iran Pause Holds
items.summary: Brent crude fell over 5 to 8 percent on Monday and continued lower Tuesday toward the mid-80s after the US paused strikes on Iran and Tehran reciprocated, opening space for Oman-brokered diplomacy. The pause followed military advice on dwindling targets and air-defense stocks. Lower energy prices reduce inflation pressure and free up room for easier financial conditions. This is classic risk-on fuel for Bitcoin and equities if the calm persists, though any collapse in talks could reverse it overnight.
items.impact: Eases inflation and boosts risk appetite if de-escalation sticks

items.title: Iran Fortifies Kharg Island Oil Terminal
items.summary: Iran is accelerating safety, fire detection, and infrastructure upgrades at Kharg Island, which handles about 90 percent of its oil exports, amid ongoing US threats to bomb or seize the facility. Dark fleet tankers continue loading there under the naval blockade. Even with the current pause, Trump has posted AI images of strikes on Kharg. Traders should note that any move against this terminal would spike oil sharply and reignite full risk-off conditions across markets.
items.impact: Keeps latent supply-shock risk elevated for energy markets

items.title: Magnitude 7.1 Quake Strikes Southern Japan
items.summary: A powerful 7.1 magnitude earthquake hit Kumamoto Prefecture on Kyushu, registering the maximum intensity on Japan's scale, knocking out power, damaging roads and a mall, and injuring dozens with a tsunami advisory issued. Japan is a major industrial and financial hub, so significant damage can ripple into supply chains, insurance markets, and the yen. For global traders it is a sudden risk event that can drive short-term safe-haven flows even if it is not a classic geopolitical conflict.
items.impact: Potential short-term safe-haven bid and supply-chain noise
